descriptions.12factor: Assess applications against Twelve-Factor principles when explicitly requested. Produce factor-by-factor gaps and modernization guidance. Exclude generic code, security, reliability, and CI/CD reviews.
descriptions.Presentations: Read, create or edit PowerPoint or Google Slides decks. Use for presentation, slide deck, PowerPoint, PPT, PPTX, or Google Slides requests.
descriptions.Spreadsheets: Create, edit, analyze, or visualize spreadsheet files and Google Sheets, including formulas, formatting, charts, and recalculation. Use excel-live-control for an active Excel session.
descriptions.actions-fcurves: Use when a Blender task involves actions, F-curves, keyframes, drivers, NLA, animation. Part of the Blender reference router; covers actions, F-curves, keyframes, drivers, the NLA, and animation behavior.
descriptions.addons-panels: Use when a Blender task involves add-ons, panels, properties, operators, UI. Part of the Blender reference router; covers add-ons, UI panels, properties, and operator-driven UI integration.
descriptions.adr: Maintain an existing ADR collection: discover conventions, create or supersede decisions, repair numbering and indexes, and review decision history. Use for decision-set maintenance rather than an isolated architecture document.
descriptions.agentwrite: Writing documents for agents. Use when creating or editing skills, or modifying AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.
descriptions.analyze-data-quality: Assess whether structured data, query results, dashboards, or analytical evidence are trustworthy enough to use. Use when the task is to check data quality, reconcile conflicting sources or metric definitions, or decide whether evidence is safe to cite.
descriptions.animqa: Validate Blender animation renders using contact sheets, silhouette stability, flicker, framing, layer separation, motion coherence, and export compatibility. Use after rendering or when the user reports poor animation quality.
descriptions.arch: Sketch types, signatures, and module boundaries before substantial implementation. Use for architecture requests or when immediate coding would commit to an uncertain design; continue coordinating as implementation progresses.
descriptions.ask: Interview the user when requested, or when missing purpose, audience, success criteria, or constraints prevent useful work. Use grill for adversarial plan review. Exclude clear mechanical requests and customer research.
descriptions.assess-patch-risk: Assess an immutable patch or commit range for runtime impact, regressions, test coverage, recoverability, and merge eligibility. Produce a read-only risk assessment; do not modify or merge the patch.
descriptions.atlas: Map Blender parts to their own texture-atlas regions. Use for exact atlas fitting, stretched textures, alpha decals, lightmaps, and textured mascot or logo exports.
descriptions.attack-path-analysis: Trace security findings from source to sink and calibrate severity during attack-path analysis or on explicit request. Do not use as the entry point for repository or diff scans.
descriptions.b3d: Orchestrate Blender creation from natural language, selecting skills for modeling, materials, lighting, cameras, animation, rendering, and export. Use for complete 3D creation tasks. Requires the official Blender Lab MCP extension.
descriptions.banim: Animate Blender objects, cameras, lights, and properties using keyframes, easing, shape keys, drivers, and NLA. Use for motion, loops, fades, pulses, morphs, facial expressions, and lip sync.
descriptions.bcam: Compose Blender shots with cameras, focal length, depth of field, tracking, and camera motion. Use for framing, cinematic shots, close-ups, overhead views, orbits, and dolly moves.
descriptions.bdoc: Look up Blender Manual and Python API facts for scripting, animation, materials, nodes, cameras, lighting, rendering, linked libraries, and add-on UI. Routes to six reference skills. Exclude other 3D tools.
descriptions.beads: Track tasks, dependencies, ownership, and completion in repositories already configured for Beads, especially across sessions or agents.
descriptions.bexp: Export Blender scenes to GLB/glTF, FBX, OBJ, USD, or STL. Configure textures, axes, geometry optimization, and platform compatibility for web, AR, game engines, VFX, or 3D printing.
descriptions.bflow: Plan complete Blender scenes and production renders across modeling, cameras, lighting, materials, rendering, and export. Use for tasks spanning several production stages, including critique, time budgets, and recovery.
descriptions.blight: Light Blender scenes using studio setups, HDRI environments, cinematic lighting, color temperature, and shadow control. Use for lighting requests, professional presentation, mood, golden hour, or rim lighting.
descriptions.bmat: Create Blender PBR materials with Principled BSDF and procedural textures. Use for metals, glass, plastic, fabric, skin, wood, coatings, or changes to roughness, shine, transparency, and surface appearance.
descriptions.bmcp: Use for inspecting or editing Blender scenes through the official Blender Lab MCP server, including bpy scripting, materials, rendering, and GLB/glTF export.
descriptions.bmesh: Create and edit Blender meshes using primitives, extrusion, bevels, modifiers, booleans, and bmesh. Use for object modeling and geometry changes; use wire3d for tracing orthographic drawings.
descriptions.bounds: Apply when wiring validation, error handling, or framework adapters. Concentrate guards at system boundaries (CLI, config, network, external APIs); trust internal types and keep business logic in pure functions.
descriptions.brender: Render Blender images or animations with Cycles or EEVEE. Configure samples, denoising, light paths, color management, and output formats. Use when producing or saving rendered results.
descriptions.bro: Restate the last message in plain human language, with no jargon.
descriptions.bsync: Coordinate Blender skills across production stages. Resolve activation conflicts, define handoffs and dependency checks, and reconcile reference accuracy with general workflows. Use for overlapping skills or repeated workflow failures.
descriptions.build-dashboard: Build source-backed dashboards for monitoring performance, exploring drivers, or acting on product and business metrics. Use when the task needs a dashboard, scorecard, or monitoring view with clear metrics, filters, source definitions, and QA.
descriptions.build-report: Build polished analytical reports for executive, product, business, or technical audiences. Use when the task needs a durable answer-first narrative with evidence-backed findings, visuals or tables, caveats, and source context.
descriptions.buv: Unwrap and texture Blender meshes, map atlases, project decals, bake textures or lighting, and prepare GLB/glTF assets. Use for texture packs, UV layouts, exact fitting, or stretched textures.
descriptions.c7: Retrieve library documentation with Context7 when implementing or checking an external library API, configuration option, or version-specific behavior.
descriptions.cameras-lights: Use when a Blender task involves cameras, lights, rendering, render engine, EEVEE, Cycles. Part of the Blender reference router; covers cameras, lights, the render engines, and rendering behavior.
descriptions.cd: Use when the user asks to design or improve deployment pipelines, release strategies, GitOps delivery, environment promotion, rollback, or coordination of application and database releases. Do not trigger for isolated CI configuration, live incident investigation, or application architecture design.
descriptions.clarity: Apply when reviewing or shaping code that's hard to trace. Count layers between question and answer, and hidden state in the reader's head; collapse one-caller wrappers and shrink mutable scope.
descriptions.cli: Use RTK and Snip to compress shell command output, select a supported wrapper, or recover complete failure details.
descriptions.contour: Build Blender surfaces from image contours or masks for exact silhouettes, mascot reconstruction, wireframe fills, or shallow reliefs. Use when the front outline must match a reference before adding depth.
descriptions.control-chrome: Control the user's Chrome browser for tasks that depend on existing Chrome state: tabs, logged-in sessions, or extensions. Prefer purpose-built connectors, APIs, or CLIs when available.
descriptions.control-in-app-browser: Control the in-app browser: navigate, inspect pages, click, type, capture screenshots, and test local websites. Existing signed-in sessions may be available. Prefer dedicated connectors or APIs for semantic resource operations.
descriptions.create-data-context: Create, update, inspect, or repair Data Analytics semantic layers. Use when the user asks to save data context or create a semantic layer that future Data Analytics work can inspect and cite.
descriptions.ctx: Retrieve original agent sessions and code provenance when prior decisions, attempts, constraints, or tool calls matter. Use before resuming earlier work or investigating unfamiliar changes; inspect cited history before relying on it.
descriptions.db: Design new or substantially redesigned relational schemas, including entities, keys, constraints, normalization, and data types. Use dbref for compatible schema migrations. Exclude isolated query tuning and SQL review.
descriptions.dbref: Change existing database schemas while preserving data and application compatibility. Handle renames, splits, type changes, constraints, backfills, and coordinated migrations. Exclude new schema design and isolated query tuning.
descriptions.debug: Diagnose unknown software failures: crashes, wrong results, hangs, races, leaks, or intermittent behavior. Use diag for difficult regressions requiring reproduction or bisection. Exclude already localized fixes.
descriptions.deep-research: Use only when the user asks for deep research (or a clear equivalent), invokes $deep-research, or selects Deep Research in Work mode. Produce a comprehensive, cited artifact. Skip ordinary research requests.
descriptions.deep-security-scan: Run repeated independent Codex Security scans and aggregate validated findings for explicitly deep or exhaustive repository audits. Use for repositories or scoped paths, not pull requests or diffs.
descriptions.define-security-policy: Create, review, or update SECURITY.md for a repository or component. Clarify security review scope, exclusions, required properties, and whether existing guidance still matches the code.
descriptions.design: Evaluate software architecture, service and module boundaries, integration, consistency, deployment tradeoffs, and architectural evolution. Exclude low-level refactoring, relational schema design, and documentation-only tasks.
descriptions.design-kpis: Design KPI frameworks, metric definitions, targets, guardrails, and measurement plans for product or business decisions. Use when success metrics, drivers, guardrails, targets, or the measurement approach need to be defined or improved.
descriptions.diag: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.
descriptions.documents: Create, edit, redline, or comment on Word and Google Docs-targeted .docx files. Render pages and inspect layout before delivery. Use for document artifacts requiring visual verification.
descriptions.domain: Apply when writing stateful logic, or when code branches a lot or repeats a shape assumption across files. Encode the domain in a structure instead of scattered conditionals.
descriptions.excel-live-control: Control an active Excel workbook through the ChatGPT add-in or connected session. Use when Excel is tagged or an established live task continues. Exclude standalone files and Google Sheets.
descriptions.explore: Apply when facing a novel UI interaction or architectural decision with no precedent in the codebase. Build 2-3 competing prototypes and compare side by side before committing.
descriptions.finding-discovery: Discover candidate vulnerabilities during the finding-discovery phase or on explicit request. Use repository and code evidence. Do not use as the entry point for full repository or diff scans.
descriptions.fitopt: Turn Blender fit reports into repair steps for geometry, textures, lighting, and projection. Use after reference validation fails; prioritize corrections and identify missing skill guidance before rebuilding.
descriptions.fix-finding: Use when the user explicitly asks to fix and verify a validated or plausible security finding. Do not use as the primary trigger for full PR, commit, branch, patch, or repository scans.
descriptions.foundations: Apply before writing logic: choosing core types and data structures, sequencing scaffold-vs-feature work, asking what concurrent actors share. Get the data structures right so downstream code becomes obvious.
descriptions.gather-business-context: Gather missing business context, metric definitions, changes, and source information before analysis. If the request also needs diagnosis or a deliverable, continue to that workflow after gathering context.
descriptions.gdpr: Apply GDPR engineering practices when designing or reviewing personal-data processing: identity, consent, logging, retention, deletion, exports, encryption, and privacy controls. Use for explicit GDPR assessments or software handling personal data.
descriptions.grill: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.
descriptions.grillme: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design.
descriptions.handoff: Compact the current conversation into a handoff document for another agent to pick up.
descriptions.how: Explain how code works, including architecture, runtime flow, ownership, and module placement. Use for walkthroughs and onboarding before changes. Use why for design motivation.
descriptions.hr: Compress large raw tool outputs, logs, JSON, or retrieved documents with Headroom, and retrieve the original before relying on omitted details.
descriptions.htk: Retrieve public web documentation with HyperText Token Killer and remove HTML boilerplate. Use for explicit tool requests or cleaned documentation. Exclude PDFs, JSON, authenticated pages, and tasks requiring JavaScript or the original DOM.
descriptions.hud: Animate Blender orbital HUD elements, halos, arcs, and markers using a reference's proportions and visual language. Use for restrained decorative motion around logos or mascots.
descriptions.idem: Apply when designing commands, lifecycle steps, or processing loops that run amid crashes, restarts, and retries. Converge to the same end state regardless of partial prior runs.
descriptions.imagegen: Generate or edit raster images from prompts or references: photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, and cutouts. Use for bitmap output; prefer existing SVG, vector, or HTML/CSS assets when those fit the task.
descriptions.index: Route Data Analytics plugin requests to the appropriate workflow for data, metrics, dashboards, reports, charts, notebooks, spreadsheets, KPIs, market sizing, or semantic layers.
descriptions.isolate: Apply when concurrent actors might write to the same file, branch, key, or state object. Eliminate the sharing first; serialize structurally only when one shared writer is a real invariant.
descriptions.jupyter-notebooks: Create, edit, or validate reproducible SQL or Python notebooks. Use for notebooks, SQL/Python scratchpads, reproducible exploration, audit trails, or runnable companions where the analysis should be reviewable or rerunnable.
descriptions.kpi-reporting: Prepare KPI readouts, scorecards, WBR/MBR/QBR updates, and executive summaries from quantitative business or product metrics; use when the task is to report status, compare against targets, explain validated drivers, and state operating implications.
descriptions.landmark: Validate and repair Blender models against named reference landmarks, proportions, and view-dependent depth. Use when bounding boxes or silhouette overlap miss important feature alignment.
descriptions.lazy: Apply when refactoring, evaluating diff size, or tempted to add abstractions, layers, or signal threading. Bias toward deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem.
descriptions.lessons: Apply when you catch yourself writing the same instruction a second time, or notice a recurring correction. Encode the rule as a lint, metadata flag, runtime check, or script instead of more text.
descriptions.lever: For substantial edits, migrations, analyses, or checks, build a reusable tool or reproducible verification instead of repeating manual work. Keep the tool small enough for a reviewer to rerun.
descriptions.linked-libraries: Use when a Blender task involves linked libraries, append, link, library override, assets. Part of the Blender reference router; covers linking and appending data, library overrides, and reusing assets across .blend files.
descriptions.look: Calibrate Blender materials, lighting, framing, glow, and color management against reference images. Measure brightness, color, silhouettes, and framing when the render's appearance differs from the source.
descriptions.market-sizing: Estimate market, segment, or opportunity size with transparent assumptions and uncertainty. Use for TAM/SAM/SOM, sizing scenarios, or comparing the scale of possible opportunities.
descriptions.mascot: Reconstruct Blender mascots, logos, or brand characters from orthographic references and textures. Use when exact brand fidelity is required. Coordinate source measurements and validation gates throughout reconstruction.
descriptions.material-nodes: Use when a Blender task involves materials, shader nodes, geometry nodes, textures, images, UV. Part of the Blender reference router; covers materials, shader and geometry nodes, textures, images, and UV data.
descriptions.mem: Retrieve or record durable decisions, discoveries, and handoff state using the configured Engrim or Engram backend.
descriptions.merge: Use when you need to resolve an in-progress git merge/rebase conflict.
descriptions.metric-diagnostics: Diagnose why a metric changed or differs from expectation. Use when the task is to identify likely drivers of a metric movement, anomaly, gap, or discrepancy.
descriptions.migrate: Apply when introducing a new internal API while old callers still exist. Migrate callers and delete the old API in the same wave instead of preserving compatibility layers.
descriptions.mvfit: Compare Blender models against multiple reference views and iteratively repair mismatches. Use when all views must meet measured silhouette, proportion, alignment, and edge criteria before export.
descriptions.mvsolve: Check whether multiple orthographic references can describe one rigid Blender model. Resolve conflicting silhouettes, proportions, part counts, and depths; establish canonical constraints before reconstruction.
descriptions.nav: Choose and use code intelligence tools when tracing symbols, assessing cross-file impact, refactoring, or discovering code structurally.
descriptions.needs: Plan customer research, analyze interviews, and identify workflows, unmet needs, or requirements before choosing a solution. Exclude routine prompt clarification, formal specification writing, and validation of an already chosen idea.
descriptions.notify: Speak a notification with say before asking the user a question or handing over a completed task, including a finished plan or verified change. Apply at these moments regardless of the task domain.
descriptions.openai-docs: Find current official guidance on Codex, ChatGPT, OpenAI APIs, models, pricing, configuration, and troubleshooting. Use for OpenAI product questions, including questions about this coding agent. Exclude generic software tasks.
descriptions.ortho: Register front, side, back, and top references into shared Blender coordinates. Use before adding depth or when a reconstruction fails to align across orthographic views.
descriptions.outcome: Apply during planned rewrites and migrations with explicit phase boundaries. Converge on the target architecture; don't preserve smooth intermediate states with throwaway compatibility code.
descriptions.pdf: Read, create, inspect, render, and verify PDF files where visual layout matters, including fillable AcroForms. Use Poppler rendering plus Python tools such as reportlab, pdfplumber, and pypdf for generation and extraction.
descriptions.perf: Diagnose Linux latency, throughput, saturation, stalls, swapping, I/O, packet loss, and resource regressions. Use for host or process performance investigations; exclude application-only profiling, SQL tuning, and generic shell questions.
descriptions.perfect: Use when the user explicitly requests a PERFECT code review, a structured self-review, or team review conventions based on PERFECT. Use code-review for a generic branch, PR, or work-in-progress review against a fixed point when PERFECT was not requested.
descriptions.pgopt: Optimize PostgreSQL queries and data structures using JSONB, arrays, custom types, ranges, full-text search, window functions, and extensions. Use when PostgreSQL-specific capabilities matter.
descriptions.pgrev: Review PostgreSQL code for correctness, security, performance, and idiomatic use of JSONB, arrays, custom types, functions, schemas, and row-level security.
descriptions.plugin-creator: Create or update personal Codex plugins, manifests, marketplace entries, and plugin directories. Handle local development, cache refresh, and reinstallation. Use when the user requests plugin authoring or changes.
descriptions.plugin-management: Discover relevant plugins, inspect permissions and dependencies, and manage connections or removal. Use for plugin questions or tasks requiring external services unavailable through current tools.
descriptions.polars: Use Polars for Python tabular analysis and transformations: loading, filtering, joins, aggregation, windows, time series, and pandas migration. Prefer lazy execution. Exclude Polars Cloud, distributed, and GPU administration.
descriptions.pony: Review code specifically for over-engineering: unnecessary abstractions, dependencies, speculative flexibility, and duplicated standard-library features. Report what to remove and what replaces it. Use for simplification or complexity reviews.
descriptions.proceed: Apply when tempted to ask 'should I do X?' on reversible work. Proceed, present the result, let the human course-correct after the fact; reserve confirmation for irreversible actions.
descriptions.product-business-analysis: Analyze product or business metrics to support decisions, prioritization, segmentation, change evaluation, and tradeoffs. Use when recommendations depend on quantitative evidence.
descriptions.propose-security-hardening: Propose structural security improvements from findings, disclosures, incidents, or completed scans. Compare alternatives and implementation tradeoffs. Use for systemic hardening requests or when the scan workflow requires hardening recommendations.
descriptions.proto: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.
descriptions.prove: Apply after completing a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact (run the feature, read the actual value, inspect the diff), not a proxy, self-report, or 'it compiles.'
descriptions.publish-artifact-to-sites: Publish validated analytical reports or dashboards through Sites. Use automatically in Work Mode when the full lifecycle is available; outside Work Mode, require an explicit publishing request or accepted sharing offer.
descriptions.pystd: Create or redesign standalone Python helpers bundled with skills, using only the standard library. Exclude project scripts, libraries, services, notebooks, and minor edits. Use pyuv for project automation.
descriptions.python-api: Look up Blender Python API behavior for bpy scripting, operators, add-ons, extensions, templates, and command-line automation. Part of the Blender reference router.
descriptions.pyuv: Create or redesign standalone project scripts using uv and PEP 723. Use for repository automation, maintenance, or data processing. Exclude skill helpers, packages, services, notebooks, minor edits, and scripts requiring no uv.
descriptions.recall: Reconstruct recent work from chat history, live state, and shared records. Use when asked to recall progress, summarize a handoff, or establish where work stopped before resuming.
descriptions.ref: Refactor code while preserving behavior: extract functions, rename symbols, split large classes, improve types, and reduce complexity. Use for focused maintenance rather than a complete rewrite.
descriptions.ref3d: Reconstruct Blender assets from reference sheets, orthographic drawings, textures, or branding with exact visual fidelity. Use for strict matching and repairs after reference mismatch. Requires Blender MCP and image-analysis tools.
descriptions.refine: Improve Blender results after poor quality, failed validation, or repeated mistakes. Diagnose gaps, repair the artifact or reusable skill guidance, validate again, and publish changes only when authorized.
descriptions.refplan: Investigate and plan a refactor across multiple files. Define scope, sequence, and verification before proposing the plan. Wait for confirmation before implementing the planned changes.
descriptions.refqa: Measure references and Blender renders before claiming an exact match. Validate silhouettes, landmarks, part counts, textures, and exports for branding or reference-driven reconstruction.
descriptions.res: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.
descriptions.rethink: Apply when integrating a new requirement into an existing design. Redesign as if the requirement had been a foundational assumption from day one, instead of bolting it on.
descriptions.roots: Apply when debugging. Trace each symptom to its root cause and fix it there; reproduce first, ask why until you reach it, resist nil-check guards that silence crashes.
descriptions.secdesign: Design security architecture, threat models, secure APIs, identity flows, privilege boundaries, and security requirements before implementation. Exclude repository scanning, vulnerability validation, exploitation, and privacy-only reviews.
descriptions.secrev: Audit code for vulnerabilities by tracing data flows and component interactions. Cover injection, authentication, authorization, secrets, cryptography, dependencies, and business logic. Use for security review requests.
descriptions.security-diff-scan: Review a pull request, commit, branch diff, or working-tree patch for security vulnerabilities.
descriptions.security-scan: Run a standard single-pass Codex Security audit of a repository, package, or path. Use when no diff is being reviewed. Route deep audits and pull-request or working-tree reviews to their dedicated workflows.
descriptions.segment: Segment overlapping visual parts from source images, wireframes, texture atlases, and decals before mesh reconstruction. Use when a mascot/logo/template contains touching or overlapping components and exact structural part masks are needed before contour, UV fitting, or landmark repair.
descriptions.simplify: Refactor given method `${input:methodName}` to reduce its cognitive complexity to `${input:complexityThreshold}` or below, by extracting helper methods.
descriptions.sites-building: Use Sites to build websites, including landing pages, portfolios, dashboards, portals, trackers, hubs, and internal tools. Always use Sites when the project contains `.openai/hosting.json`.
descriptions.sites-hosting: Host websites with Sites. Always use after `sites-building`, and use for website publishing, deployment, hosting management, or projects containing `.openai/hosting.json`.
descriptions.skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources.
descriptions.skill-installer: Install Codex skills from a curated catalog or GitHub repository, including private repositories. Use when the user asks to list available skills or install a selected skill.
descriptions.skillrev: Review agent skills for activation, readiness, value, and task quality. Design or assess trigger evaluations. Review-only requests do not authorize edits. Exclude ordinary code, security, and performance reviews.
descriptions.spec: Turn the current conversation into a spec and publish it to the project issue tracker — no interview, just synthesis of what you've already discussed.
descriptions.sqlopt: Universal SQL performance optimization assistant for comprehensive query tuning, indexing strategies, and database performance analysis across all SQL databases (MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Oracle). Provides execution plan analysis, pagination optimization, batch operations, and performance monitoring guidance.
descriptions.sqlrev: Review SQL across database engines for security, correctness, maintainability, and performance pitfalls. Check injection, access control, query patterns, and coding standards. Use sqlopt for focused tuning.
descriptions.sre: Define or assess service reliability: SLIs, SLOs, error budgets, alerts, capacity, overload, dependency failures, and recovery. Exclude live root-cause investigations and host performance diagnosis.
descriptions.steps: Break multi-step work and stacked changes into small, ordered units with verifiable outcomes. Check each unit before proceeding so reviewers can follow and validate the delivery sequence.
descriptions.subtract: Apply when sequencing an addition, refactor, or rewrite. Remove dead code, redundant validators, and stub references first, then build on the simpler base.
descriptions.tdd: Use only when the user explicitly asks for TDD, a failing test, or a regression test, OR when the bug has an obvious cheap local test target. Skip when the test path is unclear, expensive, integration-heavy, or not requested.
descriptions.teach: Explain completed work or a subsystem in plain language, combining how it works with why it was designed that way. Use for teaching requests that need understanding beyond a status summary.
descriptions.template-creator: Create or update reusable personal Codex artifact-template skills from reference documents, slides, spreadsheets, images, or other artifacts. Use for reusable template requests, not one-off creation from an existing template.
descriptions.tests: Design test coverage, choose test levels, assess suite quality, and replace brittle mocks. Use for testing strategy questions. Exclude routine test execution and unknown bug diagnosis; use tdd for test-first implementation.
descriptions.texanim: Animate transitions between Blender textures, decals, lightmaps, or visual states. Validate alignment, smoothness, and export compatibility; avoid crude crossfades, popping, and transitions unsupported by the target engine.
descriptions.texfit: Fit Blender mesh boundaries to texture-atlas regions or decal contours before UV and material work. Use when geometry should match the texture instead of stretching the texture onto an approximate shape.
descriptions.threat-model: Create or update a repository threat model during the threat-modeling phase or on explicit request. Do not use as the primary trigger for repository, pull-request, commit, or diff scans.
descriptions.tiger: Apply TigerStyle or TigerBeetle coding constraints when explicitly requested or adopted by the repository. Cover bounded work, startup allocation, and assertions. Exclude ordinary coding tasks without that policy.
descriptions.track-findings: Track validated security findings in Linear, Jira, GitHub issues, or draft advisories. Check duplicates and preview writes before approval. Handle one finding or an explicitly selected batch; exclude scanning and fixing.
descriptions.triage-finding: Assess supplied vulnerability reports or security tickets for repository impact using static evidence. Use for imported findings from scanners or trackers. Exclude vulnerability discovery, validation, exploitation, and generic bug triage.
descriptions.unslop: Cut AI tells from any writing. Must always apply.
descriptions.uvcover: Ensure textures cover every visible Blender surface, including caps and sidewalls. Use when rotation reveals gaps, back textures are incomplete, or different surfaces need separate UV treatment.
descriptions.validate-data: Validate whether an analysis is accurate, well-supported, and ready to share or use for a decision. Use when reviewing methodology, calculations, comparisons, visuals, caveats, or conclusions.
descriptions.validation: Validate candidate security findings during the validation phase or on explicit request. Determine whether vulnerabilities are real and supported by evidence. Do not initiate full repository or diff scans.
descriptions.verify-fix: Verify that a security fix remediates a reported vulnerability only when explicitly requested. Exclude ordinary tests, non-security fixes, candidate validation, and full scans.
descriptions.visualize: Create inline visualizations and interactive tools for explanations, simulations, maps, charts, comparisons, mockups, and adjustable scenarios. Use when visual exploration helps answer the request.
descriptions.visualize-data: Design, build, revise, or QA quantitative charts and figures. Use when an analytical answer needs visual judgment, whether for an inline answer, report, dashboard, notebook, or artifact.
descriptions.vulnerability-writeup: Turn vulnerability notes, disclosure reports, PoCs, source code, or Codex Security findings into self-contained, sceptically validated, natural-sounding vulnerability reports. Use for one vulnerability or a disclosure campaign; a Codex Security scan is optional.
descriptions.why: Explain design motivations and tradeoffs using source history, decisions, incidents, documentation, and operational evidence. Use for rationale, regressions, postmortems, or threshold choices. Use how for runtime behavior.
descriptions.wire3d: Convert orthographic wireframe drawings into Blender meshes and GLB/glTF exports. Use for technical front, side, back, or top views requiring reference-based reconstruction. Requires Blender MCP and Python image-analysis tools.
descriptions.write: Layered write standard: Diátaxis structure, Google developer style sentences, STE instruction rules, Global English syntax. Use for /write or when writing or reviewing docs, RFCs, readmes, PR descriptions, or commit messages.
descriptions.wt: Create, reuse, or hand off an isolated Git worktree when the user requests one or isolation has a concrete benefit for the task. Routine work stays in the current checkout.
